description: Chapter 8 - Time-independent perturbation theory. The chapter develops non-degenerate and degenerate cases before applying the method to van Vleck susceptibility and the Stark effect.

topics.title: Time-independent perturbation theory: chapter roadmap
topics.note: The chapter separates non-degenerate and degenerate spectra, then applies the resulting energy corrections to magnetic susceptibility and the Stark effect.

topics.title: Non-degenerate case: overview
topics.note: Starting with a non-degenerate unperturbed Hamiltonian, expand the energy and vector in powers of the perturbation strength.

topics.title: Non-degenerate case: first-order energy and vectors
topics.note: The diagonal matrix element gives the first energy correction, while off-diagonal elements determine the first correction to the vector.

topics.title: Non-degenerate case: second-order energy and vectors
topics.note: Second-order corrections contain energy denominators and matrix elements connecting the reference state to the other unperturbed states.

topics.title: Degenerate case: overview
topics.note: Degeneracy makes the non-degenerate denominators divergent; complementary projection operators separate a degeneracy domain from the remaining states.

topics.title: Degenerate case: first-order energy
topics.note: Diagonalize the reduced perturbation within each degeneracy domain to obtain the zeroth-order combinations and first energy corrections.

topics.title: Degenerate case: second-order energy
topics.note: The second-order correction is a sum over states outside the selected degeneracy domain.

topics.title: Application: van Vleck susceptibility
topics.note: Expand the field-dependent energy, obtain the magnetic moment and use the thermal average to obtain susceptibility.

topics.title: Application: Stark effect
topics.note: A constant electric field perturbs the degenerate Hydrogen spectrum; selection rules determine the non-zero matrix elements.

topics.title: Chapter synthesis: time-independent perturbation theory
topics.note: Choose the correct unperturbed basis, identify degeneracy before using denominators, then obtain the required corrections and physical observable.
